findings.title: New crypto provider added to the test-only artifact, not the public authz-client module
findings.body: The artifactId of this module is `keycloak-authz-client-tests`, and its own description explicitly states this module is only for the Keycloak testsuite and that 3rd parties should use `org.keycloak:keycloak-authz-client`. Yet the PR adds the new AuthzClientCryptoProvider implementation, its ASN.1 encoder/decoder, and the META-INF/services registration file into this same test-only module's `src/main`. If the public `keycloak-authz-client` artifact does not pick up this provider (it is a separate module), then the actual fix for issue #32962, which affects 3rd-party users of authz-client, never reaches them — the goal described in the PR (sync to keycloak-client repo for 3rd-party use) will not be met since this code lives in the test-only artifact.

findings.title: Multiple CryptoProvider detection no longer throws, silently picks highest-order one
findings.body: Previously, detecting more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath threw an IllegalStateException to prevent ambiguous/misconfigured deployments. The change now silently selects the provider with the highest `order()` and only logs the others at debug level. This is a behavior change that can mask accidental inclusion of multiple incompatible crypto providers (e.g. both FIPS and non-FIPS, or an unexpected AuthzClientCryptoProvider on the server classpath) which previously would fail fast; now it will silently proceed with whichever provider happens to have the highest order, potentially using the wrong crypto backend without any visible error at normal log levels.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() does not actually return a BouncyCastle provider
findings.body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` calls `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which returns the provider associated with the JVM's default keystore type — this has nothing to do with BouncyCastle and will typically return the SUN provider, not a BC provider. The method name and interface contract promise a BouncyCastle (FIPS or non-FIPS) provider; returning an unrelated provider is misleading and could break callers that rely on this contract (e.g. code registering/relying on BC algorithms via this provider).

findings.title: Dead code building unused ASN1Encoder instances
findings.body: In `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, the lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create ASN1Encoder objects, write to them, and then discard them without using the result. This is leftover/dead code that does nothing useful, wastes allocations, and is confusing to readers trying to understand the actual encoding logic that follows just below.
